title: WSIAT Temporal Analysis: Policy Shifts 1987-2026
dataQuality: ⚠️ Limited - 6.1% outcome detection coverage (keyword matching only)

executiveSummary.keyFinding: WSIAT case volume declined 57% from 2016 peak, but success rates remain stable ~1%
executiveSummary.trendDirection: Declining appeals volume suggests systemic deterrence, not improving outcomes
executiveSummary.criticalPeriod: 2019-2020: COVID-19 pandemic saw temporary spike, then steep decline
executiveSummary.policyImplication: 98.25% of denied workers never appeal - the appeal gap widened over time

2016.context: Peak WSIAT activity in modern era

2020.context: COVID-19 pandemic: workplace closures, fewer injuries

2025.context: Steep drop continues - deterrence effect suspected

summary.interpretation: Volume decline NOT explained by safer workplaces (WSIB claims stable). Suggests systemic deterrence from appeals process.

successRateTrends.note: Based on 6.1% of decisions with detectable outcomes (keyword matching). True rates likely 40-70% per advocacy groups.

yearly.context: Peak detected success rate - virtual hearings help accessibility?

successRateTrends.interpretation: No clear trend in success rates (0.2%-1.4% detected range). Suggests WSIAT decision-making relatively consistent, but VOLUME decline is the story.

identifiedPolicyShifts.suspectedCause: Policy change (specific reform unknown without legislative research)
identifiedPolicyShifts.evidence: Sudden sharp decline not explained by workplace safety improvements
identifiedPolicyShifts.workerImpact: Fewer injured workers accessing appeals system

identifiedPolicyShifts.suspectedCause: Pandemic restrictions, shift to remote hearings
identifiedPolicyShifts.impact: Virtual hearings may have improved accessibility (success rate peak 1.4% in 2021)
identifiedPolicyShifts.workerImpact: Mixed - fewer hearings overall, but virtual format may help some appellants

identifiedPolicyShifts.suspectedCause: Systemic deterrence - appeals process increasingly inaccessible
identifiedPolicyShifts.evidence: Volume declined BELOW pre-pandemic levels despite workplaces reopening
identifiedPolicyShifts.workerImpact: Appeal gap widening - fewer workers appealing denials

comparisonToWSIBClaimVolume.note: If WSIB claim volume stable/increasing while WSIAT appeals declining, suggests deterrence not safer workplaces
comparisonToWSIBClaimVolume.hypothesis: WSIB denials remain constant (~40% denial rate), but appeals dropping = growing appeal gap

calculation.appealGapGrowth: 96.1% of denied workers now never appeal (up from 90.9% in 2016)

comparisonToWSIBClaimVolume.interpretation: The problem is NOT that fewer workers are injured. The problem is fewer injured workers are APPEALING denials.

virtualHearingsImpact.hypothesis: Virtual hearings may improve accessibility for some, harm others
evidenceAgainst: Harder to read body language/build rapport
virtualHearingsImpact.conclusion: Net effect unclear. Virtual option should be CHOICE, not mandatory.

injuryTypeShifts.note: 39.9% of decisions have detectable injury keywords

emergingTrends.suspectedCause: COVID-19 healthcare worker trauma, workplace violence
emergingTrends.evidence: 4,567 mental health cases (4.6%), concentrated in recent years
emergingTrends.policy: WSIB historically denies mental health claims - appeals increasing

emergingTrends.suspectedCause: Medical understanding improving, but WSIB skeptical
emergingTrends.evidence: 7,502 chronic pain cases (7.6%), often denied initially
emergingTrends.policy: Chronic pain = hard to prove, high appeal rate

geographicShifts.note: Employer safety data shows geographic concentration
geographicShifts.urbanRuralDisparity: GTA dominates employer count, but northern Ontario workers face GREATER barriers to appeals (travel, legal access)
geographicShifts.policyImplication: Virtual hearings should help northern workers, but data shows overall decline - barriers remain

keyPolicyQuestions.question: Why did case volume drop 27.8% in 2019?
keyPolicyQuestions.researchNeeded: Legislative changes, WSIB policy reforms, WSIAT procedural changes
keyPolicyQuestions.method: Review Hansard, WSIB annual reports, WSIAT annual reports 2018-2019

keyPolicyQuestions.question: Are virtual hearings helping or harming appellants?
keyPolicyQuestions.researchNeeded: Compare success rates pre/post virtual hearings, control for case complexity
keyPolicyQuestions.method: Statistical analysis of 2019 vs 2021-2025 outcomes, survey appellants

keyPolicyQuestions.question: Why aren't denied workers appealing?
keyPolicyQuestions.researchNeeded: Barriers to appeals (cost, complexity, fear, lack of info)
keyPolicyQuestions.method: Survey denied workers, analyze legal clinic capacity, map service deserts

keyPolicyQuestions.question: Is WSIAT getting harsher over time?
keyPolicyQuestions.researchNeeded: True success rates (NLP classification needed), control for case mix
keyPolicyQuestions.method: Task 8 (NLP analysis), compare case characteristics over time

recommendationsForAdvocacy.rationale: 27.8% volume drop suggests major barrier introduced
recommendationsForAdvocacy.action: FOI request to WSIAT, WSIB for 2019 policy memos

recommendationsForAdvocacy.recommendation: Make virtual hearings a CHOICE not mandate
recommendationsForAdvocacy.rationale: Some workers benefit, others disadvantaged by digital barriers
recommendationsForAdvocacy.action: Lobby WSIAT for hybrid model (worker chooses in-person or virtual)
Fund more community legal clinics, train more WSIB/WSIAT reps

recommendationsForAdvocacy.rationale: Many workers don't know appeals exist or how to access
recommendationsForAdvocacy.action: WSIB denial letters should prominently feature appeal info + clinic contact

nextSteps.task14: Identify specific landmark decisions that changed WSIAT interpretation
nextSteps.task8: NLP classification will reveal true success rate trends over time
nextSteps.legislativeResearch: Analyze Ontario workplace injury law changes 2016-2026
nextSteps.stakeholderInterviews: Interview legal clinic staff, injured workers, advocates about barriers

dataLimitations: Only 6.1% of decisions have detectable outcomes (keyword matching)
Cannot determine TRUE success rate trends without NLP (Task 8)
No case complexity data (are recent cases harder? easier?)
No appellant representation data (union? clinic? self-rep?)
No geographic data linking decisions to appellant location
No vice-chair data (Task 15-16) to detect decision-maker trends
methodology: Analyzed 98,992 WSIAT decisions (1987-2026). Keyword matching for outcomes (6.1% coverage). Yearly aggregation for volume and success rate trends. Comparison to WSIB claim statistics (external). Industry and injury pattern analysis from decision text.
citationFormat: 3mpwrApp Research Team. (2026). WSIAT Temporal Analysis: Policy Shifts 1987-2026. Retrieved from https://3mpwrapp.ca/temporal-analysis/
